messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer acme-corp flagged a sharp p99 regression for streaming vs non-streaming. p99 TTFB jumped ~1.8s starting ~2026-03-14 16:10 UTC. Creating thread to track.

maria: Can you paste the dashboard snapshot and a sample request? is this for a single route or many? :eyes:

alex: Route is /v1/chat/stream (model: redwood-open-1-7b). Attached snapshot: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~300ms, p99 ~2.05s. Only seen on streaming path; non-streaming total time is stable.

kevin: Any recent deploys to streaming runtime or edge proxy? I saw a small h2 proxy change yesterday.

alex: deploy bot shows `deploy-service` to edge-proxy rolled 2026-03-14T15:58 by ops-ci. No dedicated runtime deploys.

julia: quick repro I ran from eu-west: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream` — got first chunk at ~1.9s. Non-streaming returned in 350ms. Will paste logs.

alex: log excerpt from edge-proxy (truncated):
```
[15:58:02.123] conn#451 start request /v1/chat/stream tenant=acme-corp
[15:58:03.987] runtime backend id=rt-42 queued 45ms, started request
[15:58:04.114] runtime responded headers, bytes=8
[15:58:04.115] edge-proxy flush-window waited 1.8s before first-chunk forward
```

sre-bot: alert: streaming-ttfb-regression tenant=acme-corp p99=2.05s threshold=1s

maria: Hypotheses: 1) edge-proxy coalescing/windowing change (deploy) 2) h2->http2 multiplexing/backpressure causing delayed flush 3) KV-cache cold leading to backend delay but non-streaming unaffected.

kevin: I can revert the proxy change to test, but need a canary plan. Suggest: rollback edge-proxy for requests from acme-corp only (tenant-scoped routing) and measure p99 over 10m. If revert not possible, enable per-tenant non-streaming fallback (force sync) as hotfix.

julia: For reproduction: I ran 10 requests back-to-back. Streaming first-chunk times: [1.92s, 1.88s, 1.95s, 300ms, 1.9s, 2.0s, 320ms, 1.85s, 1.9s, 330ms] — looks bimodal. Observed when backend RT node had concurrent continuous-batch size >8.

alex: Good data. Kevin, can you try tenant-scoped rollback canary for 50m? Maria, please open a support escalation to acme-corp with repro steps and temporary mitigation: switch to non-streaming mode or set client to poll.

kevin: Starting rollback canary now (route filter tenant=acme-corp -> previous proxy config). Will update in ~15m with metrics.

maria: Escalation note drafted and sent. Included repro curl, sample timestamps, and suggested temporary config: `x-redwood-force-sync: 1`. Customer acknowledged and said they'd flip if we confirm.

sre-bot: deploy-rollout: edge-proxy rollback canary started by kevin at 2026-03-14T16:12:10Z.

kevin: Canary metrics after 12m: streaming p99 reduced from ~2.05s -> 360ms for that tenant. p95 stable. Looks like proxy deploy was the likely cause. Rolling full rollback.

alex: Nice. Post-mortem action items: 1) add tenant-scoped rollback runbook 2) add synthetic streaming-first-chunk alert (TTFB p99 over 1s) 3) add automatic nonstream fallback flag for affected tenants 4) audit edge-proxy flush-window defaults and ensure backward-compatible deploy.

julia: I'll create a small test harness to reproduce the bimodal behavior with different batch sizes and push to eng-runtime board.

maria: Closing loop with customer: notified, they verified improvement after we flipped to sync fallback while rollback completed. They want a short write-up.

alex: thanks everyone. changing channel to #postmortems once we write up. :thumbsup:
